facts.claim: Freqtrade documentation describes spot trading, futures for selected exchanges, spot-mode no-shorting, fee-inclusive backtesting, exported trade analysis, lookahead analysis and protection controls; these are declared software capabilities, not independent performance evidence.
Hummingbot V2 separates controllers that consume market data and emit executor actions from self-managing executors; Gateway is documented as middleware standardizing blockchain and DEX interactions.
Jesse docs list spot and derivatives exchange adapters, state spot does not support short selling, and provide backtest result statistics with a caution against evaluating on net profit alone.
LEAN docs describe risk management altering portfolio targets before execution and local backtest result storage; they characterize the engine as open-source, data-agnostic and multi-asset.

OctoBot docs describe asyncio producer-consumer architecture, multi-pair/timeframe historical-data collection and backtesting against selected strategies/evaluators/configuration; named exchange coverage does not establish pair-level eligibility or DEX support.

Official dated project evidence includes Freqtrade release 2026.8 on 2026-08-31, Hummingbot 2.15.1 in June 2026, Jesse changelog 3.2.3 dated 2026-09-27, OctoBot strategy docs dated 2026-07-30, and a QuantConnect docs changelog entry dated 2026-09-09.

The reviewed evidence does not confirm simultaneous BTC, ETH and SOL spot availability for any specified venue, region, account, network or date, and does not demonstrate audited profitable multi-agent production operation or native BETTEX proposal/governance workflow support.
Jesse's stated superlative about backtest accuracy and OctoBot's speed/scalability language are vendor claims requiring independent validation.

gaps: No Tier 1 or Tier 2 source was found for independent performance/validity comparison; all cited feature evidence is first-party Tier 3.
No source verifies actual live BTC/ETH/SOL spot market eligibility by venue, region, account, quote asset, chain/token contract, liquidity or current operational status.
No common independent tests compare fees, slippage, partial fills, latency, historical data, backtest bias, or execution quality across frameworks.
Hummingbot Gateway DEX role is documented but eligible pairs/chains are not; Condor was excluded due absent documentation; OctoBot DEX/on-chain support was not established.
Native BETTEX proposal schema, independent Treasury/Risk approvals, decision preservation and financial-cycle lineage were not documented in these products.
No first-party recent OctoBot release/shutdown evidence was established; feature-page freshness is unknown where publication date is not provided.
implications: Treat these products as separable strategy/research/execution components, not as proof of proposal qualification or financial governance.
Keep spot-only/no-leverage mode and actual venue/instrument eligibility as explicit, independently verified configuration gates; product-level spot support alone is insufficient.

Use backtests, dry-run/paper workflows, lookahead diagnostics and historical result exports as evidence inputs only; require independent checks of fees, slippage, data integrity and out-of-sample behavior.
Preserve BETTEX proposal terms and independent Treasury/Risk decisions outside a bot's own strategy/execution state unless an integration is separately documented and validated.
No technology, chain, venue, platform or provider is selected by this research.
